newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bonos pulled higher by U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bonos pulled higher by U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Spain's debt market recovered early losses to end slightly firmer on Tuesday after U.S. Treasuries climbed on weaker-than-expected June NAPM data.

The U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index slipped to 55.7 in June versus 57.1 in May. Focus remains on the U.S. Federal Reserve's FOMC meeting although a Reuters poll showed that economists predicted no rate change.

"Before the U.S. data, our market was depressed by the supply following the (Spanish) Treasury auction early today," a dealer said. He added a similar trend was likely on Wednesday due to the auction of five- and 15-year bonds.
"I expect the allocation to be around 225 billion pesetas for the five-year segment, and around 50/75 billion for the 15-year bonds," the same dealer added.
The Spanish Treasury's target is for a total of 250 bln.
Six-month bills will also be offered at the auction.

"I do not expect the supply pressure to last for a long time. Maybe today the market was weaker than I was expecting yesterday but I do think it can really move out of the current tight trading range," another dealer with a U.S. house said.
The long bond future was seen oscillating between strong support at around 116.44 and resistance at 117.17.
The 10-year spread of bonos versus Bunds widened to 70 basis points from 67 basis points earlier this morning.
Dealers added it was likely the spread would remain in a narrow range between 65 basis points and 72/73 bps.
